dataset_name: NASA GPM IMERG Late Run Daily Multi-Year Historical Archive (2015–2024)
operational_monitoring_separation: This file is strictly a historical research archive (2015–2024) for antecedent rainfall analysis and model benchmarking. Operational real-time monitoring must use a separate scheduled near-real-time ingestion pipeline (IMERG Early/Late V07B via Earthdata + IMD AWS gauges).
product_version: GPM IMERG Late Run Daily (V06B archive via SERVIR ClimateSERV datatype=26)
units: mm/day (daily accumulation) and mm (3d/7d/15d rolling sums)

aggregation_semantics.antecedent_3d: Strict sum of [t-2, t-1, t]; null if any day missing
aggregation_semantics.antecedent_7d: Strict sum of [t-6 .. t]; null if any day missing
aggregation_semantics.antecedent_15d: Strict sum of [t-14 .. t]; null if any day missing
aggregation_semantics.missing_data_policy: Missing observations stored strictly as null; zero extrapolation or cross-product substitution.

study_area: Dima Hasao District, Assam (Pilot Bounding Box Areal Mean)

continuous_valid_span.post_2024_06_01_gap_explanation: SERVIR ClimateSERV datatype=26 serves the retired IMERG V06B Late Run stream ending 2024-06-01. Bridging 2024-06-02 to present requires direct NASA Earthdata Login access to GPM_3IMERGDF.07 (V07B).

direct_nasa_earthdata_v07_status.note: HTTP 302 redirect to NASA Earthdata Login (URS). Configure free EARTHDATA_TOKEN to bridge post-2024-06-01 V07B records.
direct_nasa_earthdata_v07_status.setup_instructions: Register free at https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov, approve 'NASA GESDISC DATA ARCHIVE', generate a bearer token, and export EARTHDATA_TOKEN in backend/.env.

chirps_v2_daily.source: UC Santa Barbara CHIRPS v2.0 Daily via SERVIR ClimateSERV (datatype=0)

ecmwf_era5_open_meteo.source: ECMWF ERA5 Historical Archive via Open-Meteo

steep_terrain_uncertainty_notes: GPM IMERG (0.1° / ~11.1 km) averages precipitation over ~120 km² grid cells, smoothing localized orographic cloudbursts along narrow Barail escarpments (Haflong–Jatinga–Mahur).
Passive microwave retrievals in steep, vegetated monsoon mountains suffer from warm-rain orographic underestimation and high-ice-scattering overestimation.
IMD 0.25° gridded rainfall and Assam SDMA/IMD ground rain-gauge (AWS/ARG) series are still required for local bias correction before operational threshold calibration.
attribution: NASA GSFC GPM IMERG via SERVIR Global ClimateSERV; independent references: UCSB CHIRPS v2.0, NASA LaRC POWER (MERRA-2), and ECMWF ERA5 via Open-Meteo.
